subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are a = 2j − k and b = −i + k.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the area of a parallelogram from its sides.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a×b
steps.margin_note: First mark. Area from SIDES is the magnitude of their cross product — no halving. Both vectors have a missing component; write the zeros in.
lines: Given sides a = 2j − k, b = −i + k

recall.must_convey: That the cross product of the two adjacent sides is computed, giving 2i + j + 2k.
accept: cross the two sides to get two i plus j plus two k
take a cross b using the determinant with the zeros written in
the cross product of the adjacent sides is two i plus j plus two k
rendu sides cross cheste two i plus j plus two k
heard_as: two i plus j plus two k

steps.why: The magnitude of a cross product IS the area of the parallelogram spanned by the two vectors — that is what a cross product means geometrically.
common_mistakes: Missing the zero i component of a or the zero j of b.

steps.label: Take the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Area from adjacent SIDES has no factor of a half — that factor belongs to a triangle, and to the diagonals form.

recall.must_convey: That the area is the magnitude of the cross product, √9 = 3 square units, with no halving.
accept: the area is the magnitude which is root nine equals three square units
take the modulus to get three square units, no half here
the area is three square units
magnitude three vasthundi, half avasaram ledu

steps.why: Sides give the parallelogram directly. The half only appears for a triangle, or when the DIAGONALS are given instead — as in the next question.
